title: Ghat Ramayan, Part 1 (Ghat Ramayan Bhag 1)
author: Tulsi Sahib of Hathras (c. 1763-1843)
edition_cited: Belvedere Steam Printing Works, Allahabad, 1916 (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.483643; Hindi OCR, legible)
tradition: Sant Mat (Tulsi Sahib, precursor of Radhasoami)
locator_hints: Section 'भक्ति का वरनन', file lines c. 3675-3730: surat fixed at the til, star, lightning, five colours, jyoti like a lamp, inner moon, stars, midday sun
summary: Tulsi Sahib's verse treatise. In the section on bhakti he gives a seen-light sequence for surat-shabd practice: attach the surat moment by moment, without a blink's break, to the sesame-seed point (til) at the black lotus; dwelling in the til window, a single star appears at the sky-door and the unstruck sound is heard; lightning flashes; as the surat moves toward the door the light grows; white and black, then five colours (black, red, white, yellow, green); then tej and jyoti like a lamp seen through a temple door; the jyoti bursts and a full moon appears within, then many stars, then a light like the midday sun, in which the whole cosmos is seen inside.
why_relevant: The classical Sant Mat source of the til-star-moon-sun sequence later taught by Radhasoami and Kirpal Singh.
notes: OCR has many dropped matras; anchors are copied with OCR errors intact.
